results.system_description: Heisenberg, 6√3 × 6√3 (tilted) · J = 1 · periodic · Sz = 0. H = J sum_<ij> S_i · S_j; spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2; J = 1; no constant shift
results.source_location: Table III (tab: triangular energy), row J2/J1 = 0, N = 108, column GCNN (main.tex l.418)
results.eligibility_evidence: Variational energy of the GCNN on the 108-site cluster; the Graph NN column is quoted from Kochkov et al. and excluded.
results.notes: Spin-1/2 J1-J2 model, energies in units of J1 per spin (table caption). The paper does not describe the 108-site cluster. The script dimerdimer3L2.py in the arXiv source of this version builds the 3L^2 = 108-site cluster with L = 6 as nk.graph.Lattice(basis_vectors = [[1,0],[3/2,3**0.5/2]], extent = [3*L, L], max_neighbor_order = 2), i.e. periodic along (18, 0) and (9, 3 sqrt(3)). These span the same superlattice as the instance's T1 = (9, 3 sqrt(3)) and T2 = (9, -3 sqrt(3)) of Kochkov et al., since (18, 0) = T1 + T2, and its first and second neighbors are the instance's. The script loads the saved 108-site GCNN in the Hilbert space of total Sz = 0 (nk.hilbert.Spin(total_sz = 0)) with exchange sampling. Plain GCNN with 8 layers of 6 feature maps, trained with 4096 samples for about 2000 steps (Sec. Triangular-lattice J1-J2 model). <S^2> = 0.131(4) in the same row.

results.notes: Spin-1/2 J1-J2 model, energies in units of J1 per spin (table caption). The paper does not describe the 108-site cluster. The script dimerdimer3L2.py in the arXiv source of this version builds the 3L^2 = 108-site cluster with L = 6 as nk.graph.Lattice(basis_vectors = [[1,0],[3/2,3**0.5/2]], extent = [3*L, L], max_neighbor_order = 2), i.e. periodic along (18, 0) and (9, 3 sqrt(3)). These span the same superlattice as the instance's T1 = (9, 3 sqrt(3)) and T2 = (9, -3 sqrt(3)) of Kochkov et al., since (18, 0) = T1 + T2, and its first and second neighbors are the instance's. The script loads the saved 108-site GCNN in the Hilbert space of total Sz = 0 (nk.hilbert.Spin(total_sz = 0)) with exchange sampling. Residual GCNN with 12 blocks of six feature maps, trained with LayerSR on 4096 and then 16384 samples (Sec. Triangular-lattice J1-J2 model). <S^2> = 0.208(7) in the same row.

results.eligibility_evidence: Variational energy of the state obtained by one Lanczos step on the residual GCNN, the lowest eigenvalue of the Hamiltonian in the two-dimensional Krylov space (appendix 'Implementation of the Lanczos step'); the exact/interpolated value and the Graph NN column are excluded.
results.notes: Spin-1/2 J1-J2 model, energies in units of J1 per spin (table caption). The paper does not describe the 108-site cluster. The script dimerdimer3L2.py in the arXiv source of this version builds the 3L^2 = 108-site cluster with L = 6 as nk.graph.Lattice(basis_vectors = [[1,0],[3/2,3**0.5/2]], extent = [3*L, L], max_neighbor_order = 2), i.e. periodic along (18, 0) and (9, 3 sqrt(3)). These span the same superlattice as the instance's T1 = (9, 3 sqrt(3)) and T2 = (9, -3 sqrt(3)) of Kochkov et al., since (18, 0) = T1 + T2, and its first and second neighbors are the instance's. The script loads the saved 108-site GCNN in the Hilbert space of total Sz = 0 (nk.hilbert.Spin(total_sz = 0)) with exchange sampling. One Lanczos step applied to the residual GCNN of the GCNN column (Sec. Triangular-lattice J1-J2 model and appendix 'Implementation of the Lanczos step').
